claims: In most rooms that carry these steps, a member starts a mark, members then call for hands, members then build and report the mark, and members then keep it (N01).
Keeping a mark brings a room into talk with other rooms: border talk with neighbours, requests for help, and coalitions under attack (N02, N09).
A call to place can turn into a call to attack a rival's work, and other members of the same room answer it with a refusal that gives a reason, a truce, or continued taunting in talk (N03).
Members join a call with a bare one-line answer, while refusals come with a reason, and the account borrows this pattern from conversation analysis (A12, F-014).
Members settle a design with a posted template and do not decide how they are organized; a leader, vote or oath appears in only 46 of 705 rooms (N07, C01).

After a mark is reported done, members celebrate it, record it and carry the record on into banners, later canvases and groups; placement stopped at hour 73, and after it members curate the record (N04).
Calls to the canvas come before the host sub draws a line around canvas talk, such as a megathread or removals (N05).
Under upkeep strain, members turn to scripts and spare accounts, and rooms that judge they have too few hands move to a new spot (N06, N08).
April Fools play ran beside the canvas work in 368 rooms and did not delay that work (K01, F-009).
relations: P02 is settled by P04 (A11, theorised, does not beat its null)
P01 is answered by P15 (A12, theorised, no order count)
K01 runs beside the work with no arrow and no effect on its timing (F-009)
C01 and C02 stand on findings and carry no arrow
P10 does not lead back to P03 (no loop)
could_not_follow: Its earlier claim, that the replies show a room its numbers, failed its test (F-015, weak).
It ranks story rooms told with no residue above a smaller count of elements.
Ten of the 16 rooms told with no residue tell the frame beside the work, so K01 was restored.
The pass 5 story told 19 of its 35 rooms with a residue, and the account cannot reach these communities:
It also breaks in late rooms that enter the canvas through another room, and in rooms whose replies the coders did not code.
This curation is apart from carrying the work on [P13], and it is not a part of making the work.
It differs from the transparent task architecture of open source, because no founder lays the work out; any member may post a template.
the completion ritual is not reward provision in Puranam and colleagues' sense.
It is not a shared basis of authority in O'Mahony and Ferraro's sense (2007), which a community builds before it can govern itself.
The field's analyst found the same in r/place.
unsupported: The opening note says each order beats its null unless called thin or theorised. The figure file shows the thin arrows A05, A10, A14 and A19 beat their nulls, and N08 says A10's one transition fails the audit, so the label thin does not mark what the note says. The counts for April Fools play (368 rooms, 88 rooms), design argument (281 rooms) and flags (96 rooms) carry no source in the packet, and the findings F-002 to F-017 are cited but not served. The sentence 'The field's analyst found the same in r/place' names no source. The claim that a template does not make placers follow it shows no count or quote. The 31 of 52 stigmergy records carry no null and no arrow. The ultrahardcore paragraph says the room had no neighbour, but the same paragraph has a member proposing to take over other works' hearts and another sparing one. The cardinals room does not fit the start-then-call order: by hour 53 the room had no logo, and a member offered to help only if someone else started one.

rooms.instead: The account fits two parts of the cardinals room. The Fanbot April Fools play ran from h16.79 to h21.80 (K01). Members also joked about a rival Cubs logo (t05), which is close to the pre-canvas rivalry claim C02. The account's main chain does not fit. The chain needs a starter (R01) and then calls for hands. In the cardinals room, a member asked at h53.78 'Why no cardinals logo on /r/place?'. Another member answered with a conditional pledge: 'If someone gets it started, I'll help after the game.' That pledge is not a bare answer to a call. It waits for a starter who had not appeared. For most of the canvas, the room watched a rival's mark and wished for its own. The seven sampled passages show no build report and no upkeep.

The seven sampled luciomains passages show most of the N01 and N04 chain. 'GREAT IDEA' at h13.03 is a bare one-line answer to a rally (P01, P15). 'Here's the spray' at h25.53 shares what to build (P02, P04). Two passages fix single pixels in the lettering at h26.89 and h51.36, which is upkeep (P05) and the stigmergy pattern of naming what the mark lacks. 'you guys are the best' at h61.50 is celebration (P11). The account itself lists luciomains among the rooms it cannot reach. The leftover part is visible: members turned the canvas work into Lucio and Overwatch game jokes, at h51.30 and h72.62. The account names that as what the mark brought back to the room, and it gives that no element.

The mysterydungeon room is a late room: its first coded passage is at h52.62. Within it, the account's chain shows. Two call posts at h52.62 give coordinates and ask for a hand (P01). A celebration thread follows at h55.25 (P11). At h69.02 a post asks members to check the mark and fix wrong pixels (P05), and a reply at h69.06 reports 'It's already being overtaken.' The room's theme title 'moving the Time Gear' suggests a move (P10), but no sampled passage voices doubt about hands (K02). In this room, celebration came before upkeep, the reverse of the account's order from building to upkeep to celebration. Guild and time gear jokes ran beside the work.

declarations.sentence: In-group humour, or culture as such: the construct holds only the traffic between a frame the room had and the new episode.
declarations.why: The word 'only' bounds what the construct gathers and claims nothing about what the rooms did, so the rule needs no support for it.

declarations.sentence: Each account could place one pixel per interval, and no one could order another to place.
declarations.why: Both clauses restate setting facts from the contract: one pixel per interval for each account, and no authority over another's placing.

declarations.sentence: The form pass found such lines and never counted them.
declarations.why: The word 'never' describes the analyst's own procedure and not the rooms or members, so the rule does not reach the sentence.

declarations.sentence: Here no one could hold a member's time or assign it.
declarations.why: The setting fact covers authority over placing only, and holding or assigning a member's time is a wider universal claim with no count or finding.

declarations.sentence: The calls here rarely offer anything beyond the work: a reward offered before the work appears in 9 of 705 rooms (F-016), for example 'As an insentive, for every person who joins in and comments below I will post 5 pig gifs!
declarations.why: The finding F-016 and the count of 9 of 705 rooms support it, and a member's quote shows the act.

declarations.sentence: In six rooms or fewer each, they adopt a sign others began, make a tribute alone, build memorials to the dead, leave the work unsigned, plan a mark that moves in the timelapse or follow the creator's wishes. 483 of 705 rooms carry at least one of these: 'Does it bother anyone else that the logo is off center.....' [smite/c0348].
declarations.why: The comparative 'fewer' rests on counts of rooms carrying each theme (six or fewer, 483 of 705) and a member's quote.

declarations.sentence: Two rooms or fewer each defy the call for restraint, mourn art the room covered, place rival marks together or urge repair over retaliation. 205 of 705 rooms carry at least one of these: 'We mean you no harm!
declarations.why: The comparative 'fewer' rests on counts of rooms carrying each theme (two or fewer, 205 of 705) and a member's quote.

declarations.sentence: In six rooms or fewer each, a room stays neutral, members negotiate across a language gap, argue whether cooperation is surrender or trade away another room's work. 467 of 705 rooms carry at least one of these.
declarations.why: The comparative 'fewer' rests on counts of rooms carrying each theme (six or fewer, 467 of 705).

declarations.sentence: Members say themselves that an agreement does not bind every placer: 'Their group has agreed to not mess with our space but there will always be those individuals who don't listen / care' [hentai/c0105].
declarations.why: The universal 'every' rests on the setting fact that no one holds authority over another's placing, and a member's quote states it.

declarations.sentence: Members work out who changed their work and why.
declarations.why: The sentence uses the causal word 'why' and carries no count, finding, setting fact or member's quote, so the rule calls for a rewrite.

declarations.sentence: In three rooms or fewer each, members plant disguised scripts on rivals, brigade one person off Reddit or relay a streamer's call to attack. 231 of 705 rooms carry at least one of these.
declarations.why: The comparative 'fewer' rests on counts of rooms carrying each theme (three or fewer, 231 of 705).

declarations.sentence: In some rooms, a tie from before the canvas names the rival in the same turn as the attack (C02, untested for order; F-013: 10 turns in 7 story rooms), and membership carried in does not come before the attack more often than chance (F-011).
declarations.why: The two findings F-013 and F-011 support it, and the sentence makes no order claim beyond them.

declarations.sentence: Frame analysis would cover every interpretation in the corpus; this names only the host community's handling of its own space during the event.
declarations.why: The words 'every' and 'only' compare the scope of a literature construct with the scope of the dimension and claim nothing about what the rooms did.
